verdict.rationale: Cursor's own Automations feature runs cloud agents in the background. They fire on a recurring schedule (presets or cron) or on events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Linear and more. Cursor-managed agents (Bugbot, Security Agents, PR Routing & Approval) and isolated cloud VMs let these agents build, test, fix and open PRs autonomously. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that scheduled or triggered automations reliably maintain and fix code in practice.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: Cursor Automations run cloud agents in the background, either on a schedule or in response to events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Linear, and more.
Scheduled triggers take "preset options or ... a cron expression"; source-control triggers cover PR opened/pushed/merged, push-to-branch, comments, labels.
Set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to build, maintain, and fix your software.
The `/automate` skill lets you describe the workflow you want in plain language. Cursor configures the automation's triggers, instructions, and tools for you.
